findings.title: Electron consumer killed by a signal (crash/OOM/timeout kill) exits the runner with code 0
findings.evidence: run-consumer-electron.ts:204-206 registers `child.on('exit', (code) => process.exit(code || 0))`. Node passes `code === null` and a non-null `signal` when a child dies from a signal, so `null || 0` gives 0. The sibling run-consumer-snap.ts:110-114 handles this as `process.exit(signal ? 1 : (code ?? 1))`, and utils/external-consumer.ts:105 maps a signal to 1. The Electron runner drops the signal argument entirely.
findings.impact: If the Electron consumer segfaults in a native addon, is OOM-killed (SIGKILL), or is killed by a CI timeout (SIGTERM), `run-consumer-electron` exits 0. CI and orchestrators then count a crashed consumer run as a success, which hides real native crashes in the QVAC SDK under Electron.
findings.reproduction: Point the electron consumer config at an app whose main process runs `process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGSEGV')` (or run `kill -9` on the Electron PID while it runs). Run the run-consumer-electron command with --skip-build and check `echo $?`: it prints 0.
findings.fix: Use `child.on('exit', (code, signal) => { if (signal) console.error(`❌ Electron consumer terminated by signal ${signal}`); process.exit(signal ? 1 : (code ?? 1)) })`, matching run-consumer-snap.ts.
